theory.intro: To **add** two vectors, draw them tip to tail. The **resultant** runs from the tail of the first arrow to the tip of the last. To subtract, add the negative.
facts: The **negative** $-\underset{\sim}{b}$ has the same length as $\underset{\sim}{b}$ but points the opposite way.

Subtraction is not commutative in general: $\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}=-(\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{b})$. If $\underset{\sim}{a}=\underset{\sim}{b}$, both differences are the zero vector.
In column form, add or subtract the top components and the bottom components separately.
steps: Rewrite any subtraction as adding the negative
Join the vectors tip to tail
Read the resultant from the first tail to the last tip

workedExamples.solution_text:
Add corresponding components.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\begin{pmatrix}4\\-3\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}-7\\8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}4+(-7)\\-3+8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}-3\\5\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$
Subtract corresponding components.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\begin{pmatrix}4\\-3\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}-7\\8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}4-(-7)\\-3-8\end{pmatrix}\\&=\begin{pmatrix}11\\-11\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Given $\underset{\sim}{a}=2\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}=-6\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$, find $\underset{\sim}{a}+\underset{\sim}{b}$, $\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $3\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac{\underset{\sim}{b}}{2}$ in component form.

The resultant of $\begin{pmatrix}x\\-2\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}4\\y\end{pmatrix}$ is $\begin{pmatrix}9\\5\end{pmatrix}$.
Find $x$ and $y$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{pmatrix}x+4\\-2+y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}9\\5\end{pmatrix}$
Equate the top components.
$x+4=9$
$x=5$
Equate the bottom components.
$-2+y=5$
$y=7$

workedExamples.question_text:
In triangle $DEF$, $\overrightarrow{DE}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\overrightarrow{EF}=\begin{pmatrix}-7\\6\end{pmatrix}$.
Find $\overrightarrow{FD}$ as a column vector.
Prove that $\overrightarrow{JK}-\overrightarrow{LK}+\overrightarrow{LM}=\overrightarrow{JM}$. State the laws used.
workedExamples.solution_text:
By the negative vector law,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{JK}-\overrightarrow{LK}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JK}+\overrightarrow{KL}+\overrightarrow{LM}\end{aligned}$
Apply the triangle law twice.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{JK}+\overrightarrow{KL}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JL}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JM}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Prove that $\overrightarrow{HJ}-\overrightarrow{HK}-\overrightarrow{JK}=2\overrightarrow{KJ}$. State the laws used.
workedExamples.solution_text:
By the parallelogram law of subtraction,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{HJ}-\overrightarrow{HK}-\overrightarrow{JK}\\&=\overrightarrow{KJ}-\overrightarrow{JK}\end{aligned}$
By the negative vector law,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{KJ}-\overrightarrow{JK}\\&=\overrightarrow{KJ}+\overrightarrow{KJ}\\&=2\overrightarrow{KJ}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Prove that $\overrightarrow{RS}-\overrightarrow{US}+\overrightarrow{QR}=\overrightarrow{QU}$. Show your steps clearly and state the laws used.
workedExamples.solution_text:
By the negative vector law,
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{RS}-\overrightarrow{US}+\overrightarrow{QR}\\&=\overrightarrow{RS}+\overrightarrow{SU}+\overrightarrow{QR}\end{aligned}$
Use the commutative law to arrange a connected path.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{RS}+\overrightarrow{SU}+\overrightarrow{QR}\\&=\overrightarrow{QR}+\overrightarrow{RS}+\overrightarrow{SU}\end{aligned}$
Apply the triangle law twice.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{QR}+\overrightarrow{RS}+\overrightarrow{SU}\\&=\overrightarrow{QS}+\overrightarrow{SU}\\&=\overrightarrow{QU}\end{aligned}$

mastery.question_text:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\7\end{pmatrix}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=\begin{pmatrix}-8\\2\end{pmatrix}$.
Find $\overrightarrow{CA}$ as a column vector.
Prove that $\overrightarrow{JK}-\overrightarrow{MK}+\overrightarrow{HJ}=\overrightarrow{HM}$. Show your steps clearly and state the laws used.
mastery.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{JK}-\overrightarrow{MK}+\overrightarrow{HJ}$
$=\overrightarrow{JK}+\overrightarrow{KM}+\overrightarrow{HJ}$ by the negative vector law.
$=\overrightarrow{HJ}+\overrightarrow{JK}+\overrightarrow{KM}$ by the commutative law.
$=\overrightarrow{HK}+\overrightarrow{KM}$ by the triangle law.
$=\overrightarrow{HM}$ by the triangle law.
